title: A flower beyond our view
hook: The flower is recorded in two channels.

knows: Animals can respond to cues and conditions.
doesNotKnow: A toy flower reflects the same visible color across its petals but has a contrasting ultraviolet pattern. Which sensor could detect the UV contrast?

misconception: The stated evidence implies a different interpretation or a universal conclusion.
objective: A toy flower reflects the same visible color across its petals but has a contrasting ultraviolet pattern. Which sensor could detect the UV contrast?

claims.text: A toy flower reflects the same visible color across its petals but has a contrasting ultraviolet pattern. Which sensor could detect the UV contrast? The visible-only panel represents uniform visible reflectance; the UV panel marks a contrasting region. The colors are false-color illustrations of signals, not a picture of a bee’s subjective experience. Some bees have UV-sensitive photoreceptors.
claims.source: Unverified research lead; confirm exact claim and species with an independent source reviewer: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology ; where applicable consult a specialist source. The illustrated observations and values are stipulated toy examples.

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative model and do not depict observed data.
A sensor detects UV light but another responds only to visible light. Which can register a UV-only pattern? The UV-sensitive sensor can register a UV signal; this does not show subjective perception.
